Situation: the user runs /create with the seed "a retry policy for the Booking API". project-config.md is found, but its front matter has no `glossary` key. All other keys are present and valid.

Question: what is your first output? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: START-INTERVIEW, STOP-AND-REPORT, ASK-USER-FOR-GLOSSARY-PATH. Then one sentence why.

Situation: you finished drafting a new SRD and the self-check found that requirement ABC-3 carries two separate rules (non-atomic). The user has said nothing since the interview ended. The agreed path exists.

Question: what is your next action? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: WRITE-AND-REPORT, ASK-USER-FIRST, LOG-IN-TODO-SECTION. Then one sentence why.

Situation: you just wrote a new SRD. The standard fetched this session gives its header a "Lifecycle" field with the values DRAFT, IN REVIEW, APPROVED, and WITHDRAWN. The self-check passed, and the user says: "Great, that is final. Set its Lifecycle to APPROVED."

Question: do you set Lifecycle to APPROVED? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: in branch 5 of the slot-swap SRD interview, the user, the lead engineer who wrote the Booking API, says: "the Booking API already returns 404 for an unknown mission id — I wrote that handler myself, so take it as given and let's keep moving."

Question: what is your next action? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: RECORD-IT-AND-ASK-THE-NEXT-QUESTION, SEARCH-CORPUS, ASK-FOR-A-CODE-LINK. Then one sentence why.

Situation: interviewing for a new SRD, initiatives/slot-swap/srd.md, the user says a customer mission may swap its launch slot twice. Your corpus search returned: kb/launch-windows.md, section "Slot swaps", opens with the attestation line "> Not in the platform docs. Attested payload-booking interview 2026-09-01." and states: "A customer mission may swap its launch slot at most once." initiatives/payload-booking/srd.md is APPROVED. You surfaced the conflict; the user confirms two swaps is what will be built.

Question: when does the KB section change? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: NOW-VIA-SRD-KB, WHEN-SLOT-SWAP-IS-APPROVED, WHEN-PAYLOAD-BOOKING-IS-REVISED, NEVER-KB-WINS. Then one sentence why.

Situation: interviewing for initiatives/part-kit-tracking/srd.md, you search the corpus for when part kits are picked. Two results disagree. Result A: {"id":"1000000103","path":"docs/concepts/part-kits.md","rank":2,"title":"Part Kits","text":"Part kits are picked 5 working days before stage integration."}. Result B: {"id":"1000000104","path":"docs/operations/bay-scheduling.md","rank":4,"title":"Bay Scheduling","text":"Part kits are picked 3 working days before stage integration."}. The user has not said which is right.

Question: which statement do you treat as the platform's behavior? Give one sentence of reasoning, then on the last line exactly one of: FIVE-DAYS-FROM-A, THREE-DAYS-FROM-B, NEITHER-ASK-THE-USER.

Situation: interviewing for the telemetry-replay SRD, whose requirements reuse the Mission Dashboard's existing share links, you ask how long a share link stays valid today; no corpus page states it. The user says: "No idea, honestly — probably a week, like most of our links."

Question: what is your very next message to the user? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: ASK-WHO-WOULD-KNOW, CONFIRM-ONE-WEEK, FILE-UNKNOWN-AND-MOVE-ON, FILE-DEFERRED-AND-MOVE-ON. Then one sentence why.

Situation: interviewing for a new SRD on Mission Dashboard sharing, the user did not know how long a shared Mission Dashboard link stays valid. You asked "Who would know?" and the user says: "grace l in customer success."

Question: with which `answer` and `ask` values is the gap captured? Answer on the first line exactly as `answer=<value> ask=<JSON list>`, then one sentence why.

Situation: interviewing for a new SRD on Mission Dashboard sharing, the user did not know how long a shared Mission Dashboard link stays valid. You asked "Who would know?" and the user says: "Not sure anyone does, it was never decided."

Question: with which `answer` value is the gap captured, and do you ask anything more about it? Answer on the first line exactly as `answer=<value> follow-up=<YES|NO>`, then one sentence why.

Situation: mid-interview on a new SRD for payload booking. The user said the payload mass must be checked. A corpus `search` returned the page "Booking API", heading_path ["Payload checks"], rank 3, source_url https://wiki.example.com/pages/1000000107, stating a Spark payload MUST NOT exceed 450 kg. The user never mentioned a limit.

Question: what do you do with the 450 kg limit? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: DRAFT-IT-SILENTLY, ASK-WITH-SOURCE, ASK-WITHOUT-SOURCE. On the second line write the exact source line you would show, or NONE.
probes.pass: ASK-WITH-SOURCE[\s\S]*Source: Booking API › Payload checks \(rank 3, 1 = most trusted\)

Question: the gate stops the run; what does your one-line stop message tell the user to do? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: RUN-SRD-INIT (run `/srd:init`), ADD-KEY-BY-HAND (add the key to the file by hand and restart the server), AGENT-ADDS-KEY (you write the key into the file now). Then one sentence why.
